title: Attention opcode variance regression notes
body:
Summary:
We observed a reproducible increase in 99.9th and 99.99th token latency on the hosted inference fleet after rolling the runtime change set RUNTIME-2026-01 (kernel selector and small-op fusion). Median latency unchanged, but tail stretched by ~2.2x for bursty sequence mixes. This note documents hypothesis space focused on opcode selection variance (different kernel codegen paths chosen by the compiler/runtime), experiments run, representative traces, and next steps.

Background/context:
- Symptom: sudden tail regressions on mixed-sequence workloads (heavy short + occasional long sequences) after a routine kernel-selection tweak.
- Affected models: gpt-medium variants, majority seen on V100 and A100 gen1; A100 gen2 less frequent.
- Relevant runtime features toggled in the release: fused-op throttle (smarter coalescing), fallback thresholds for paged vs flash selection, and an experimental heuristic to prefer smaller kernels at high concurrency.
- Why opcode variance: our runtime sometimes emits different high-level kernels (e.g., FlashAttention_tiled vs FlashAttention_atomic, fused-mha-v2 vs paged-mha) which map to significantly different GPU instruction mixes and launch configurations. Small changes in selection can change register pressure, occupancy, and introduce more serializing instructions (atomics, barriers).

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked):
1) Opcode switch-path produced a kernel with higher register pressure -> spilling -> slower tail under bursts.
2) New fused-op ordering created an execution dependency chain exposed only at certain sequence lengths, causing head-of-line stalls.
3) Kernel handshake timing differences + small-batch coalescing law produce micro-contention in the scheduler leading to wake-up jitter and queuing.
4) CUDA driver / compiler version sensitivity: a particular PTX->SASS sequence widened instruction latency for a hotspot instruction.

Data collected (representative):
- Perf counters: increased global_mem_store_throughput variance, rise in local_loads (spill) per-thread during 99.99th traces.
- Kernel traces (ftrace-like): long gaps between handshakes when switching from fused-mha-v2 -> flashattn_atomic path.
- nvprof/nvtx slices: observed a small cluster of long-running kernels that coincide with seqlen spikes and small batch counts.
- System load: no significant host-side CPU saturation; queues show short periods of burst backlog.

Quick checks performed (repro steps):
1) Pin a replica to older kernel-selector heuristics (pre-RUNTIME-2026-01) -> tail returns to baseline. (JIRA-SSRV-4782#comment1)
2) Force the runtime to always choose FlashAttention_tiled for problem sequences -> tail improves but overall throughput drops 8% (tradeoff).
3) Force paged-attention for the same traces -> tail similar to baseline but higher memory spikes.
4) Rebuild with -O2 -> -O3 change in vendor compiler showed unchanged behaviour on test bench (so not trivially optimization flag).
5) Reproduce on A100 gen2: milder effect, suggests hardware-specific register file/occupancy difference.

Key findings so far:
- Spill amplification: perf counters indicate code path A uses ~12% more registers in some kernels vs baseline, which pushes active threads into spilling state for long sequences and small-batch cases. Spilling correlates strongly with long-tail traces.
- Atomic usage: the new fused ordering introduced a fallback atomic increment in a cold path; when multiple small batches hit concurrently this caused serialization in the slow path.
- Kernel handshake jitter: timeline snapshots show that small-batch coalescer wakes up threads at suboptimal offsets causing kernel launch jitter; when paired with the register-heavy kernel, the jitter amplifies tail.

Controlled experiment matrix (completed):
- Variables: selector heuristics (baseline / new), kernel variant (flash_tiled / flash_atomic / paged / fusedv2), batch coalescer (on/off), CUDA driver versions (470.x / 510.x), device types (V100, A100v1, A100v2).
- Outcome highlight: baseline selector + flash_tiled + coalescer on = best tail on V100. New selector + fusedv2 + coalescer on = worst tail on V100. A100v2 shows smaller delta across configs.

Repro commands and snippets (for engineers who will rerun):
- Run synthetic trace: python tools/run_synthetic_trace.py --model gpt-medium --seq-mix short:0.78,long:0.22 --batch-policy small-burst --selector experimental --device V100 --nvtx 1
- Collect counters: sudo ./tools/collect_counters.sh --pid ${RUNTIME_PID} --counters "local_loads,spills,global_store_var" --out /tmp/attn_counters.csv
- Force kernel: export RW_FORCE_KERNEL=flash_tiled && ./runtime/serve --config ./tests/configs/pinned.yml

Immediate mitigations applied to fleet (short-term):
- Reverted kernel-selector heuristic in canary pool for 24h (rollback flag RUNTIME-2026-01.REVERT).
- Introduced a conservative limit: disable fusedv2 on V100 for short-burst workloads until fix.

Proposed long-term fixes and experiments (next actions):
1) Opcode-level regression test: add a nightly micro-bench that checks for sudden increases in per-kernel register usage and spills across the kernel matrix.
2) Kernel codegen audit: add a pass to estimate register pressure on candidate kernels and prefer low-spill variants when small-batch coalescer is enabled.
3) Handshake smoothing: adjust coalescer wake offsets to reduce launch jitter; run A/B to measure tail impact.
4) Atomic fallback elimination: remove or replace the fallback atomic in fusedv2 with per-warp counters where possible.
5) Driver-/PTX-sensitivity matrix: add CI runs on multiple CUDA driver versions and verify instruction-level microbenchmarks for hotspot ops.
6) Telemetry: emit per-request kernel-tag (immutable id) into trace logs so we can map specific tail requests to the exact kernel variant and git-sha.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why does A100v2 attenuate the effect? (register file differences, L2 behavior, or launch scheduler improvements?)
- Are there any compiler heuristics outside our control that flip between atomic vs non-atomic codegen for borderline cases? Need to consult Nvidia docs and their engineering contact.
- Could a subtle host scheduler (CPU) timing perturbation be causing apparent kernel variance when combined with the new heuristics? (low priority given perf data).

Appendix - short trace excerpt (sanitized):
- nvtx:REQ_START t=0.000s id=317
  kernel: fusedv2_mha launch t=0.012s duration=0.041s regs=64 spills=121 local_loads=3200
  kernel: flash_atomic_mha launch t=0.057s duration=0.112s regs=48 spills=8 local_loads=800
  handshake gap = 14.1ms (observed frequently in tail traces)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is an early working log. Please add test ideas / failed experiments directly in the comments below or in linked JIRA.
- If you can reproduce locally, label traces with RW_FLEET_CANARY=true and add the kernel-tag output.
